title: Longest Run of One Letter
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. A run is a block of neighbouring characters that are all the same letter.

Return the length of the longest run in s.

examples.why: "oo", "kk" and "ee" all have length 2. The word has three e's, but they are not all next to each other.
The z's come in two separate blocks of 2 and 3. Counting every z would give 5, which is wrong.
A single letter is a run of length 1.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Scan once. What do you need to know about the run that ends at the current character?
Only its length: it grows by one if this character equals the previous one, and restarts at 1 otherwise.
Update the best answer on every step, not only when a run ends, or a run at the very end is missed.

explain.intuition:
A run ends exactly where the letter changes. So walk the string and keep the length of the current run: same letter as before, add one; different letter, start again at 1. The answer is the biggest value that counter ever reaches.

You never need to look further back than one character, which is why this is a window whose left edge just jumps to the change point.
steps: For each i from 1: if s[i] === s[i − 1], add one to run; otherwise set run = 1.
Set best = max(best, run) after each step.
pitfalls: Counting how many times a letter appears in total instead of how many appear in a row ("zzaazzz" is 3, not 5).
Only updating best when the letter changes, which misses a run that reaches the end of the string.

solutions.title: Grow a run from each position
solutions.idea: From every index, count how far the same letter continues to the right.

solutions.title: One pass with a counter
solutions.idea: Extend the current run on a repeat, reset it to 1 on a change.

followups: Return the letter of the longest run too, choosing the earliest on ties.
You may change up to k characters. How long can the longest run become?
